title: He is with you wherever you are
hookLine: He is with you wherever you are (57:4)

lines: A NEW APARTMENT, BOXES TAPED SHUT.
A SHORT LINE FOR NEW PLACES.
cards: An airport gate at 5am. A hospital corridor. A new apartment with the boxes still taped shut.
A hotel room in a city where you don't speak the language. Places like these can make a person feel strangely unhooked, as if they've left their whole life at the last address.
Surah fifty-seven, Al-Hadid, has a short line for exactly that feeling. It sits in the middle of a verse about the heavens and the Throne.

teach.h: THE FIRST, THE LAST, OUTWARD, INWARD.
teach.b: Al-Hadid opens wide: everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies God. Verse three gives four names in a row: he is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward.
Verse four describes God creating the heavens and the earth in six days, then establishing himself on the Throne.
He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out, what comes down from the sky and what goes up into it.
And then, in Pickthall: "and He is with you wheresoever ye may be." Wa huwa ma'akum ayna ma kuntum. Ma'akum: with you.
Ayna ma kuntum: wherever you are. The verse ends: and God sees what you do. So how is God with you?
Muslims have explained it in more than one way.

teach.h: BY KNOWLEDGE AND SIGHT, OR NEARNESS.
teach.b: Commentators such as Ibn Kathir said he is with you by his knowledge, hearing and sight, watching over you, while being above his Throne, as the same verse says.
Others, among them Sufi writers, dwell on the nearness itself, and read it with another verse: God is nearer to a person than their jugular vein.
Both readings agree on one thing: in the verse, no place is out of his sight. The hadith of Jibril turns this into a way of worshipping.

teach.h: IHSAN: AS THOUGH YOU SEE HIM.
teach.b: Asked what ihsan, excellence, is, the Prophet ﷺ said: to worship God as though you see him, and if you don't see him, he sees you.
The airport gate, the hospital, the empty apartment: the verse doesn't make them less strange. It says you didn't arrive there alone.

how: Some Muslims recall this verse when traveling or in unfamiliar places; the idea of ihsan, worshipping as though one sees God, is taught from the hadith of Jibril, where it follows islam and iman.

o: for you, on your side in every argument
among you, as a guest who visits the home
with you; God is with you wherever you are

games.q: Al-Hadid, verse four — tap the pairs.
p: worship as though you see him

s: the same verse mentions both the Throne and 'with you'
it describes God on the Throne and says he is with you wherever you are.
all Muslims explain 'with you' in exactly the same way
commentators such as Ibn Kathir say by knowledge and sight; Sufi readers dwell on nearness.
the verse ends by saying God sees what you do
and God sees what you do.

games.q: someone asks the Prophet what ihsan, excellence, is. what does he say?
o: to worship God as though you see him.
games.why: to worship God as though you see him, and if you don't see him, he sees you.

practice: Feel exactly where you are: the floor, the chair, the air on your skin. Breathe in: wherever; breathe out: you are.
Then picture the next unfamiliar place you'll walk into, a waiting room, a new street, and hear the line said quietly at its door.

wordCard.voice: Ma'akum: with you, the words of 57:4 that say God is with a person wherever they are. Today's word.

orig.say: wa HU-wa ma-'A-kum AY-na maa KUN-tum
orig.note: Arabic: and He is with you wherever you are. ma'a means with; ayna ma, wherever.

carryVoice: Your line: wherever you are. Even at an airport gate at 5am. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: and He is with you wheresoever ye may be.
